chunks: Muhammad ibn Aḥmad, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:

I was seated in his presence, and he was asked about a man who enters into iḥrām wearing a garment containing silk. So he called for a qurqubī loincloth and said: 'I enter into iḥrām in this, and it contains silk.'

key_terms.قُرْقُبِيٍّ: a type of fabric or garment (qurqubī)
key_terms.يُحْرِمُ: enters into the state of ritual consecration (iḥrām)

ai.seo_question: Can a pilgrim wear silk clothing during Hajj or Umrah according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kāfī highlights the practical flexibility (rukhaṣ) within Shia jurisprudence regarding the prohibition of silk during iḥrām, illustrating that the restriction applies primarily to wearing silk as a garment of luxury rather than an absolute ban on its presence. By donning a qurqubī (a type of tunic or loincloth) containing silk, Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) establishes a precedent that the material's integration into a standard garment does not invalidate the state of consecration, provided it is not worn for ostentation. This narration is frequently cited by scholars to distinguish between the general prohibition of silk for men and the specific requirements of iḥrām, emphasizing necessity and customary usage over rigid textual literalism.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Hanaan Bin Sadeyr, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I was seated in hisasws presence, and heasws was asked about a man who wears Ihraam in a cloth in which is silk. So heasws called for a Qurquby loin cloth and heasws said: ‘Iasws wore Ihraam in this and in it is silk’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Ahmad has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il from Hanan ibn Sadir who has said the following:

“Once I was sitting in the presence of abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when he was asked about a man who uses for Ihram a fabric which has silk in it. He (the Imam) asked for a loincloth made in Qurqabiy (name of a place) and said, ‘I use this for Ihram and it has silk in it.’”
